ignored.snippet: var sortedSources = sources.slice().sort(function(a,b){ return a.label < b.label ? -1 : a.
ignored.reason: Equivalent, and checked rather than argued. This mutant only changes what the sort comparator returns for two EQUAL keys (1 instead of 0). V8's Array.prototype.sort (TimSort) only ever branches on order < 0, so 1 and 0 lead to the same placement and the same final order. Verified by differential run: arrays of 2, 3, 10, 33, 70, 200 and 1000 all-equal keys, and 300 mixed keys, sorted with both comparators: identical order every time. The < to <= mutant on the same line is NOT equivalent and is killed by the stable-ties test.
